newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Dollar selling pushes Sri Lanka rupee to close up.
newsitem.headline: Dollar selling pushes Sri Lanka rupee to close up.

text.p: Inward remittances saw selling of dollars in the Colombo market which pushed the Sri Lankan rupee up against the greenback on Wednesday, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.54 to the dollar after opening at 57.63, they said. The rupee closed at 57.65 on Tuesday.
"A big inward remittance has made people rethink the value of holding dollars," said an American Express Bank dealer. "When this happens, selling (of dollars) gathers pace."

Since last week, a state bank has been unloading an inward remittance of about $16 million dollars that was received from the U.N. Compensation Commission to be paid to Sri Lankans who incurred losses during the Iraqi occupation of Kuwait, other dealers said.
"A block like this makes the market sit up and take notice, specially when it is not going anywhere," said a local bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar by quarter local cent. Buying and selling prices were fixed at 57.2210 and 58.3770.
Overnight call money closed at 11 percent with the market liquid, dealers said.
